newsitem.title: UK: Brit Airways flights disrupted by strike effects.
newsitem.headline: Brit Airways flights disrupted by strike effects.

text.p: British Airways Plc was struggling on Sunday to restore its service to full operation after a 72-hour strike by cabin staff.
Flight schedules remained disrupted as crew rosters and aircraft movements were badly disrupted by the strike and a total of 2,000 cabin crew were still off sick.
Around 200 cabin crew have contacted BA to say they are fit to come back to work, BA said in a statement.
The strike ended early yesterday but the airline was able to operate only 70 percent of its intercontinental flights out of Heathrow Airport, its main hub.
Around 45 percent of BA's European and 40 percent of its domestic services took off from Heathrow. At Gatwick Airport, BA operated 89 percent of long-haul departures.
On Monday, BA expects to run 85 percent of long-haul flights, 60 percent of European flights and more than half of its UK services.
Out of Gatwick, the airline will operate almost 95 percent of flights, and full service is expected to be restored on Tuesday, BA said.
Cabin crews went on strike over a plan by BA to save 42 million pounds ($71 million) and to restructure pay and conditions as part of a drive to sharpen its competitiveness.
